title: Long-lived stream tracing: websocket/gRPC span stitching and log/metric correlation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: We currently lose causal trace continuity for long-lived connections (WebSocket and bi-directional gRPC streams). This makes it impossible to attribute tail-latency spikes and intermittent errors to originating requests and user sessions. Goal: implement span stitching + request-anchor markers in SDK/middleware so that: 1) server and client-side stream fragments are stitched into a single logical trace, 2) logs and metrics emitted during the stream carry a stable correlation id that links to the trace, and 3) dashboards can surface stream-level tail-latency and error bursts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end trace view produced for a sample long-lived WebSocket session with correct parent-child relationships across reconnects. 2) SDK emits 'stream_anchor_id' as both span attribute and log/metric tag. 3) Trace sampling policy honored and head-span persists minimal metadata for lookup when child spans are dropped. 4) Grafana dashboard panel(s) display tail-latency (95/99/99.9) for streams and annotate error bursts with top 5 correlated services. 5) PR(s) merged, e2e test in integration pipeline, release notes added.
design_notes: High-level approach: Introduce a lightweight StreamAnchor object in language SDKs that: - creates a stable short-id for the session (stream_anchor_id), - attaches an initial head span with minimal baggage/attributes (originating_request_id, user_id if present, sampling_decision), - persists anchor metadata in in-memory weak map to support reconnects for the lifetime of the client process. For each message/frame we create short-lived child spans referencing the anchor head span. For servers that accept both HTTP upgrades and native gRPC streams, middleware adapters will detect stream start/stop and emit stream lifecycle events to the observability pipeline.
implementation_details: SDK changes: add StreamAnchor API (create/start/close) across node/python/go SDKs. Middleware: websocket adapter and grpc interceptor to call StreamAnchor.create() on new stream and StreamAnchor.close() on finalization. Propagation: use a compact header 'x-rw-stream' containing base64(short-id|flags|ttl). Sampling: if sampling decision is 'drop', still emit anchor head-span at low-cardinality (no stack or payload) to allow rollups and dashboard linking. Telemetry pipeline: ensure OTLP exporter maps stream_anchor_id -> log/metric labels and that our log processors add 'stream_anchor_id' to structured logs. Storage: tracing backend must index span attributes for stream_anchor_id for fast lookup. Dashboard queries: add prebuilt PromQL and trace explorer settings in the dashboard playbook.
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Emitting a head-span even for dropped samples increases span count slightly; mitigated by keeping attribute set minimal and sampling head span at an aggressive rate. - Adding SDK state increases memory footprint for very high connection counts; mitigated by weak references and TTL-based eviction. - Header size: compact binary header chosen to reduce wire size but requires careful compatibility testing with proxies. - Potential privacy: anchor ties logs to user identifiers; SDK will respect PII masking config and default to not including user_id unless explicitly enabled.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dogfood: enable stream tracing on staging for two low-risk services (edge-proxy and chat-backend) behind feature flag. 2) Collect metrics for span growth and memory. 3) Iterate sampling rates. 4) Gradual ramp to production for dedicated customers with notices. 5) Add dashboard panels and run an internal demo session for SRE/Support.
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for StreamAnchor lifecycle, integration test that simulates reconnect and asserts single logical trace, smoke test for log/metric correlation by emitting a test counter tagged with stream_anchor_id and verifying pipeline ingestion. Load test to validate no >5% increase in memory at 10k concurrent streams. Add trace-based alerting rule for error-burst detection tied to stream_anchor_id frequency.
